notes: na túru = (going) on a hike. Výlet = a day trip of any kind.

examples.tl: Zítra jdeme na túru na Sněžku.
examples.en: Tomorrow we're going on a hike up Sněžka.

notes: Mostly plural: hory. To the mountains = na hory; in the mountains = na horách.

examples.tl: O víkendu jedeme na hory.
examples.en: At the weekend we're going to the mountains.

notes: na vrchol = to the summit, na vrcholu = on the summit. Sněžka (1 603 m) is the highest in Czechia.

examples.tl: Na vrcholu hodně fouká.
examples.en: It's very windy on the summit.

notes: Mountain hut with beds, beer and hot food; in the Krkonoše it is a 'bouda'. Also a weekend cottage.

examples.tl: Na chatě si dáme polévku a pivo.
examples.en: At the hut we'll have soup and a beer.

notes: A coloured stripe between two white ones on trees and rocks. Red = main long routes, then blue, green, yellow.

examples.tl: Jděte pořád po červené turistické značce.
examples.en: Keep following the red trail marker.

notes: Arrow signs at trail junctions listing destinations with distances in km. The junction itself is a 'rozcestí'.

examples.tl: Na rozcestníku je napsáno: Sněžka 3 km.
examples.en: The signpost says: Sněžka 3 km.

notes: Naučná stezka = nature trail with info boards; cyklostezka = bike path. Any route is also a 'cesta'.

examples.tl: Stezka vede lesem k vodopádu.
examples.en: The trail leads through the forest to the waterfall.

notes: po + colour: po červené (red), po modré (blue), po zelené (green), po žluté (yellow).

examples.tl: Na vrchol jděte po červené, zpátky po modré.
examples.en: Take the red trail to the summit and the blue one back.

notes: Czech hills are dotted with them; a small fee, often cash, to climb. Petřín in Prague is the famous one.

examples.tl: Z rozhledny je vidět až do Polska.
examples.en: From the lookout tower you can see as far as Poland.

notes: Covers cable cars, chairlifts and funiculars. By cable car = lanovkou.

examples.tl: Na Sněžku jede lanovka z Pece pod Sněžkou.
examples.en: A cable car goes up Sněžka from Pec pod Sněžkou.

notes: Start and cíl (finish) are on every race map. Úschovna = bag drop.

examples.tl: – Kde je start? – Na náměstí, v devět hodin.
examples.en: – Where is the start? – On the square, at nine o'clock.

notes: Summer afternoon storms are common in the mountains: start early and get off the ridge in time.

examples.tl: Odpoledne mají být bouřky.
examples.en: There are supposed to be thunderstorms in the afternoon.

tl: Jak dlouho se jde na vrchol?
en: How long is the walk to the top?
accept: How long does it take to the summit?
How long is the hike to the summit?
notes: se jde = one walks. Swap the end: na chatu (to the hut), k lanovce (to the cable car).

examples.tl: – Jak dlouho se jde na vrchol? – Asi dvě hodiny.
examples.en: – How long is the walk to the top? – About two hours.

notes: těžký = difficult or heavy; lehký = easy or light; prudký = steep.

examples.tl: – Je ta cesta těžká? – Ne, jen ke konci je prudká.
examples.en: – Is the trail difficult? – No, it's only steep toward the end.

notes: Check the mountain rescue (Horská služba) forecast before a ridge walk.

examples.tl: Kazí se počasí, radši se vrátíme.
examples.en: The weather is turning, we'd better go back.

notes: Both the sport and a running event. Going for a run = jít si zaběhat.

examples.tl: Ráno si jdu zaběhat podél řeky.
examples.en: In the morning I'm going for a run along the river.

notes: běžím = I'm running (now, or a race); běhat is the habit: běhám třikrát týdně = I run three times a week.

examples.tl: Zítra běžím půlmaraton.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm running a half marathon.

notes: 1 závod, 2 závody. Big ones in Prague: the půlmaraton in spring and the maraton in May.

examples.tl: V sobotu běžím závod na deset kilometrů.
examples.en: On Saturday I'm running a ten-kilometre race.

notes: The banner over the finish line says CÍL; the start is START. Also 'destination' in navigation apps.

examples.tl: Do cíle zbývají dva kilometry.
examples.en: Two kilometres to go to the finish.

notes: 1 číslo, 2 čísla, 5 čísel. It has to be worn on the front.

examples.tl: Kde si vyzvednu startovní číslo?
examples.en: Where do I pick up my bib number?

notes: In race info and on signs at the expo; bring ID. Also called 'registrace' or 'prezence'.

examples.tl: Výdej startovních čísel je v pátek od deseti.
examples.en: Bib pickup is on Friday from ten.

notes: Runners' slang for the official 'občerstvovací stanice'. On maps it is marked 'občerstvení'.

examples.tl: Občerstvovačka je na každém pátém kilometru.
examples.en: There's an aid station every five kilometres.

notes: To the gym = do posilovny. Casual: fitko. A single visit is a 'jednorázový vstup'.

examples.tl: Je v hotelu posilovna?
examples.en: Is there a gym in the hotel?

notes: A woman says: Jsem unavená.

examples.tl: Po závodě jsem hodně unavený.
examples.en: After the race I'm very tired.

notes: 'Bolí' is the same for one thing or several. Mám křeč = I have a cramp.

examples.tl: Po maratonu mě bolí nohy.
examples.en: My legs hurt after the marathon.

notes: What Czech crowds shout at runners and at hockey. Literally 'into it'.

examples.tl: Do toho, už jen kilometr!
examples.en: Come on, only one kilometre left!
